fact: Seer is a prediction market platform that leverages Reality.eth.
quote: Seer is a prediction market platform that leverages [Reality.eth]

fact: Seer uses the Conditional Tokens Framework to create and manage various types of markets.
quote: and [Conditional Tokens Framework](https://conditional-tokens-docs.netlify.app/docs/introduction1) to create and manage various types of markets.

fact: Categorical markets let users select one outcome out of multiple options.
quote: Categorical Markets: Select one out of multiple outcomes.

fact: Multi-categorical markets allow selection of multiple outcomes.
quote: Multi-Categorical Markets: Similar to categorical market but allowing selection of multiple outcomes.

fact: Scalar markets have a numeric outcome within a specified range.
quote: Scalar Markets: Numeric outcome within a specified range.

fact: Futarchy markets are used to make decisions based on a token's predicted price.
quote: Futarchy Markets: To make decisions based on a token's predicted price.

fact: Seer uses Reality.eth as its oracle system for resolving market outcomes.
quote: Seer uses Reality.eth as its oracle system for resolving market outcomes.

fact: Reality.eth questions are submitted with parameters such as opening time, timeout, and minimum bond.
quote: Questions are submitted to Reality.eth with specific parameters such as opening time, timeout, and minimum bond.

fact: Seer supports multiple Reality.eth question templates, including single-select, multi-select, and numeric scalar questions.
quote: The system supports multiple question templates, including single-select, multi-select, and numeric (scalar) questions.

fact: Seer utilizes the Conditional Tokens framework for creating and managing outcome tokens.
quote: Seer utilizes the Conditional Tokens framework for creating and managing outcome tokens.

fact: Each market condition is prepared using the Conditional Tokens contract.
quote: Each market condition is prepared using the Conditional Tokens contract.

fact: Outcome tokens are represented as ERC1155 tokens within the Conditional Tokens system.
quote: Outcome tokens are represented as ERC1155 tokens within the Conditional Tokens system.

fact: Seer wraps ERC1155 outcome tokens into ERC20 tokens to improve usability.
quote: To improve usability, Seer wraps the ERC1155 outcome tokens into ERC20 tokens.

fact: The ERC20 wrapping allows easier trading and integration with existing DeFi protocols.
quote: This allows for easier trading and integration with existing DeFi protocols.

fact: Seer uses Kleros to resolve disputes that may arise when answering Reality.eth questions.
quote: Seer uses Kleros to resolve disputes that may arise when answering Reality.eth questions.

fact: An outcome token is a digital asset representing a specific outcome in a prediction market; each token corresponds to a particular result and can be bought, sold, or traded.
quote: A digital asset representing a specific outcome in a prediction market. Each token corresponds to a particular result and can be bought, sold, or traded by participants.

fact: Outcome token prices are not fixed — their value moves with the market's perceived likelihood of that outcome occurring.
quote: The value of an outcome token fluctuates based on the perceived likelihood of that outcome occurring.

fact: Outcome tokens are only convertible into the underlying asset once the market question is resolved.
quote: Outcome tokens can be redeemed for the underlying tokens when the question is resolved.

fact: Split (minting) converts one collateral token into a complete set of outcome tokens for a market, one token per outcome.
quote: Converting a collateral token into a complete set of outcome tokens for a market.

fact: Split is illustrated by depositing 1,000 sDAI to mint 1,000 of each outcome token in a three-outcome market.
quote: someone can put 1000 sDAI to create 1000 « sDAI if Trump », 1000 « sDAI if Biden » and 1000 « sDAI if Other ».

fact: Merge is the inverse of split: a complete set of outcome tokens is combined back into a single collateral token.
quote: Combining a complete set of outcome tokens back into a collateral token.

fact: Redeeming exchanges winning outcome tokens for collateral, normally at a 1:1 ratio, after resolution.
quote: The act of exchanging winning outcome tokens for the collateral (usually at a 1:1 ratio) after the market has been resolved.

fact: Outcome tokens are backed by collateral, typically a stablecoin, which guarantees winners can be paid at resolution.
quote: The asset (usually stablecoin) used to back the value of outcome tokens in a prediction market.

fact: Oracles are the external data mechanism that supplies the answer used to resolve a market question.
quote: For prediction markets, oracles supply the information needed to resolve markets accurately (answer market questions)

fact: Disagreement or ambiguity about the correct outcome triggers a resolution dispute, handled by a predefined dispute resolution mechanism.
quote: A situation that arises when there is disagreement or uncertainty about the correct resolution of a prediction market.

fact: Every Seer market automatically carries an invalid outcome, used when no predefined outcome accurately reflects the real result.
quote: This outcome is automatically considered for all markets on the Seer platform to account for situations where none of the predefined outcomes accurately represent the actual result.

fact: If a market resolves as invalid, invalid outcome tokens are redeemable for the underlying collateral.
quote: Invalid outcome tokens can be redeemed for the underlying collateral if the market is resolved as invalid.

fact: Scalar markets cover a continuous range and pay proportionally: DOWN tokens redeem fully at/below the minimum, UP tokens fully at/above the maximum, and both partially in between.
quote: For outcomes within the range, both token types are partially redeemed, with the proportion based on where the outcome falls within the range.

fact: Conditional markets only resolve if a condition tied to a parent market occurs, and their outcome tokens convert into parent outcome tokens only if that condition holds.
quote: If the parent market resolves in favor of the condition, these tokens can be redeemed for the corresponding parent outcome tokens.

fact: Liquidity provision works through liquidity pools, where providers earn a small fee on each trade executed in their pool.
quote: Users that provide liquidity (Liquidity Providers) take a small fee of each trade that occurs in their liquidity pool.

fact: Outcome tokens can be bought or sold from a token pool if enough liquidity exists, in addition to minting.
quote: Besides minting, you can also buy or sell outcome tokens from a token pool (provided there is enough liquidity).

fact: The buy UI places outcome choices on the left and the collateral amount entry on the right, with a Buy button.
quote: To buy outcome tokens, click on an outcome of your choice (on the left). On the right, enter the amount (sDAI or wxDAI) and click **Buy**.

fact: On Gnosis, the right-side token switch shows wxDAI or xDAI based on which the user holds more of, while sDAI is always on the left.
quote: **On Gnosis:** The switch will show **wxDAI** or **xDAI** on the right depending on which token you possess more of (it will always show **sDAI** on the left).

fact: On Ethereum Mainnet, the interface always shows DAI on the right.
quote: **On Ethereum Mainnet:** It will always show DAI on the right.

fact: If the liquidity pool lacks enough tokens, the app can block purchases that would cost more than 1 sDAI per outcome token.
quote: The above message means that you cannot spend more than 1 sDAI to buy 1 outcome token (in the example you need to pay 15.38 sDAI for 1 YES token).

fact: The maximum trading price for an outcome token is 1 sDAI per token, so buying is disabled above that to prevent definite losses.
quote: Since the maximum price at which an outcome token can be traded is 1 sDAI per token, we disable buying to prevent buyers from incurring a definite loss.

fact: Clicking Buy opens a confirmation popup for the trade.
quote: After clicking **Buy**, a confirmation popup will appear:

fact: The trade confirmation shows details including price and fee.
quote: You can check various details of the trade, including the price and fee.

fact: Trades can experience slippage between expected and actual received amounts because trading occurs on a DEX.
quote: Note that there will be slippage between what you expect to receive and what you actually receive (since we are trading on a DEX).

fact: A minimum received amount protects users from large price spikes; otherwise the trade reverts.
quote: However, there will be a minimum received amount to ensure you don't suffer from a huge price spike (it will revert otherwise).

fact: The Continue button executes the trade after confirmation.
quote: Click **Continue** to execute the trade.

fact: Selling is the reverse of buying: it swaps outcome tokens back into collateral tokens.
quote: **Selling** is the exact opposite of buying, swapping from outcome tokens to your collateral tokens.

fact: To bet on an outcome in a Seer prediction market, a user first needs to hold outcome tokens.
quote: In prediction markets, to bet on an outcome, you will need to have some outcome tokens.

fact: Outcome tokens serve two purposes: they can be traded, or redeemed for collateral tokens.
quote: These token can be traded or used to redeem for collateral tokens.

fact: Minting (also called splitting) requires the user to hold available collateral, either sDAI or xDAI.
quote: To mint (split), you must have some available sDAI (or xDAI) tokens.

fact: Minting returns outcome tokens to the user.
quote: After minting, you will receive outcome tokens.

fact: Minting is a 1:1 split against sDAI: 1 sDAI mints 1 outcome token of every outcome.
quote: 1 sDAI can mint 1 outcome token of each outcome.

fact: Because of the sDAI/xDAI exchange rate, 1 xDAI mints roughly 0.9 outcome tokens per outcome.
quote: Because of the exchange rate between sDAI and xDAI, 1 xDAI can only mint about 0.9 outcome tokens of each outcome.

fact: A mint always produces a full set of outcome tokens, not only the outcome the user wants to bet on.
quote: After minting, you will receive outcome tokens for all outcomes, not just the one you selected.

fact: Merging is the inverse operation of minting.
quote: Merge is the exact opposite of mint.

fact: Merging converts a complete set of outcome tokens back into collateral (xDAI or sDAI).
quote: You can exchange your outcome tokens for xDAI (or sDAI).

fact: Merging requires a prior token approval allowing Seer to handle the user's outcome tokens.
quote: Note that before merging, you need to allow (approve) Seer to handle your outcome tokens.

fact: Redemption is only possible after the market has been resolved.
quote: A market must be resolved (see [Resolve market](/app/resolve-market)) before you can redeem your outcome tokens.

fact: The redeem flow mirrors the merge flow in the UI.
quote: The redeem process is quite similar to merge.

fact: The docs distinguish two UI states for the redeem flow based on market resolution.
quote: **Market has not been resolved:**

fact: The documentation distinguishes terminology: minting is also referred to as splitting.
quote: To mint (split), you must have some available sDAI (or xDAI) tokens.

fact: Seer documentation is organized into separate pages, including a dedicated 'Resolve market' page.
quote: Resolve market](/app/resolve-market)

fact: Liquidity providers can provide liquidity for any outcome they choose.
quote: Users can provide liquidity for any outcome of their choice.

fact: Liquidity providers earn a proportion of the trading fees generated by the outcome they support.
quote: Liquidity providers (LP) will earn a proportion of the fees generated from trading that outcome.

fact: To provide liquidity, a user first visits a market, selects an outcome, and mints outcome tokens.
quote: First, visit any market, select an outcome and [mint outcome tokens](/app/mint-merge-redeem-outcome-tokens).

fact: Each outcome has an Add liquidity button in the Seer interface.
quote: On each outcome there will be an **Add liquidity** button.

fact: For markets without liquidity, users are directed to the Swapr site.
quote: For market that does not have liquidity, you will be directed to the Swapr site.

fact: For markets that already have liquidity, a popup appears and clicking Open directs the user to Swapr.
quote: For market that already had liquidity, a popup will appear. Click on **Open** to be directed to Swapr as well.

fact: On Swapr, users should check that the selected pair is correct.
quote: On Swapr, check if the selected pair is correct.

fact: Normally liquidity is provided in sDAI, but conditional markets use two outcome tokens.
quote: Normally, you would want to provide liquidity in sDAI. However, in conditional markets, both tokens will be outcome tokens

fact: In conditional markets, the pair consists of a conditional outcome token and the parent outcome token.
quote: (one is the conditional outcome token, and the other is the parent outcome token)

fact: Providing liquidity for a token pair requires holding both tokens.
quote: To provide liquidity for a pair of tokens, you must hold both tokens.

fact: Users set an initial price for the pair, which determines how much of each token must be provided.
quote: Set an initial price for the pair. This number will later be used to determine the corresponding amount of each token in the pair you need to provide.

fact: Swapr uses concentrated liquidity, letting LPs provide tokens within a specific price range.
quote: Swapr is based on the concept of concentrated liquidity, which allows users to provide their tokens as liquidity for trading within a specific price range.

fact: Liquidity providers earn their fee share only within the active liquidity range.
quote: Liquidity providers earn their fee share only within this active liquidity range.

fact: Users unsure about range selection can click Full Range.
quote: If you're unsure about this, click the **Full Range** button on the right.

fact: Swapr calculates the required token ratio from the initial price and selected range, and users must provide both tokens in that ratio.
quote: Swapr will calculate the token ratio based on the initial price and the selected price range. You must provide both tokens in the correct ratio.

fact: Seer markets must follow platform guidelines to ensure clarity and safety for all users.
quote: Markets created on Seer must adhere to specific guidelines to ensure clarity and safety for all users.

fact: Creators are instructed to read the Verified Markets Policy (hosted on Kleros IPFS) before creating a market.
quote: Before creating your market, please read the [Verified Markets Policy](https://cdn.kleros.link/ipfs/QmfGcodBzG53DBxS2Uxu5jug9YiHUpJ5tKFqhP6Z2HjscU/Seer%20-%20Verified%20Markets.pdf)

fact: A separate Market Resolution Policy document also exists and should be reviewed before market creation.
quote: [Market Resolution Policy](https://cdn.kleros.link/ipfs/QmW6npv4J3jvF87WVCEaQQ6f2PK1T9ytX2eYg86XkT9ScK/Seer%20-%20Markets%20Policy.pdf)

fact: Market creation is initiated from the home page via a 'Create a market' button.
quote: On the home page, click **Create a market**.

fact: The first step of the creation flow is selecting a market type.
quote: 1. **Select a market type:**

fact: The second step is entering the market question and its outcomes.
quote: 2. **Input the question and outcomes:**

fact: Multi-scalar markets require a specific question format, with the outcome type placed in brackets in place of the outcome value.
quote: Since each outcome have its own question, you should place the outcome type in brackets to replace the outcome value in the question.

fact: Multi-scalar question format example references a party-name placeholder within a 2024 U.S. Presidential Election question.
quote: How many electoral votes will the **\[party name]** win in the 2024 U.S. Presidential Election?

fact: The third creation step is specifying an opening date.
quote: 3. **Specifying an opening date. The market can only be resolved after the opening date:**

quote: The market can only be resolved after the opening date

fact: The fourth step is previewing the market, after which the creator clicks Create Market.

fact: Markets can be verified at creation time using a switch button in the 'Verify it Now' row.
quote: You can verify the market during creation by clicking the switch button in the **Verify it Now** row.

fact: Verification can alternatively be completed after the market is created.
quote: If you prefer, you can also complete the verification later.

fact: Unverified markets display a warning on the platform.
quote: Unverified market will display a warning.

fact: The Seer documentation site is built and hosted on Mintlify.
quote: This documentation is built and hosted on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com), a developer documentation platform.

fact: A Seer market can be resolved by waiting until the current reported answer becomes final.
quote: You can either wait until the [current answer](/app/report-answer) is final or [raise a dispute](/app/raise-a-dispute) and wait for a ruling.

fact: Alternatively, a user can raise a dispute and wait for a ruling before resolution.
quote: or [raise a dispute](/app/raise-a-dispute) and wait for a ruling.

fact: After the relevant status appears, the user clicks the 'Report Answer' button to resolve the market.
quote: Either way, after you see the following status, you can click on **Report Answer** to resolve the market.

fact: Once a market is resolved, holders can redeem their winning outcome tokens.
quote: The market is resolved. You can now redeem your winning tokens (YES tokens in this case).

fact: Seer outcome tokens are referred to as YES tokens for the winning outcome in the example.
quote: You can now redeem your winning tokens (YES tokens in this case).

fact: The resolution UI includes a 'Report Answer' action and displays a status before resolution.
quote: after you see the following status, you can click on **Report Answer** to resolve the market.

fact: The document notes an existing experiment in which AI agents participate in prediction markets.
quote: There is already an experiment using AI agents[^omen] to participate in prediction markets.

fact: The stated main potential of AI agent markets is high-speed, algorithm-to-algorithm participation where humans cannot practically participate.
quote: we believe the real power of AI agent markets lies in computer speed (i.e. where humans can’t participate anyways) markets used by algorithms.

fact: Machine learning is described primarily as a prediction technology, with examples such as ad clicks and movie preferences.
quote: Indeed, machine learning is mainly used to make predictions: Will the user click on this ad? Will the user like this movie?

fact: The current internet is described as dominated by services using AI to predict user behaviour.
quote: Current internet is dominated by services which are using AI to make predictions about user behaviours.

fact: If decentralized protocols replace corporate predictive engines, prediction markets are proposed as the open replacement process.
quote: there will be a need to replace those predictive engines by an open process: Prediction markets.

fact: In the social-network example, AIs submit candidate content with a very small amount of money used as liquidity for a market on whether a user will like that content.
quote: All AIs can submit potential content with a small amount of money (think less than a cent) to be used as liquidity for “Will user X like content Y?”.

fact: AIs then trade on those content markets, and the content with the highest “Yes” prediction is displayed while other markets are cancelled.
quote: AIs can then trade on those markets. Content with the highest prediction of “Yes” is displayed to the user (and other markets are cancelled).

fact: After the user interacts, markets resolve and AIs profit or lose based on whether their prediction was correct.
quote: After the user interacts, markets are resolved, so AIs who predicted that the user would like a specific content make profits if the user does and make a loss if the user doesn’t.

fact: AIs that proposed content and supplied liquidity for content the user liked receive a small reward.
quote: A small reward is also given to the AIs who proposed content (and put the liquidity) the user liked.

fact: The proposed AI-market mechanisms are said to apply across many domains.
quote: Those mechanisms can work in countless domains, here is a non exhaustive list:

fact: One listed application is predicting whether a user would interact with particular content.
quote: Predicting if a user would interact with a particular content.

fact: Another application is predicting the star rating a user would give to a business such as a shop or restaurant on a map.
quote: Predicting the amount of stars a user would give to a particular business (ex: shop and restaurants on a map).

fact: AI markets could predict the stars given to content on streaming platforms.
quote: Predicting the stars given to a particular content (ex: streaming platforms).

fact: AI markets could predict whether a user would click an ad or make a purchase related to an ad.
quote: Predicting if a user would click on an ad or make a purchase related to an ad.

fact: AI markets could predict whether users on a dating app would match and have a sustained interaction.
quote: Predicting if a user would match a user on a dating app and have a sustained interaction with this user.

fact: Seer's practical implementation has two components: an AMM and an auction system.
quote: We can see this as a system with 2 components: an AMM and an auction system.

fact: Liquidity providers interact with the AMM contract, while traders interact with the auction contract.
quote: Liquidity providers interact with the AMM contract while traders interact with the auction contract.

fact: The AMM restricts trading to the auction contract only.
quote: The AMM only allows the auction contract to trade with it.

fact: A trader buying an outcome token sends underlying tokens such as a stablecoin or sDAI to the auction contract.
quote: When a trader makes an order, trading an underlying token (ex: stablecoin, sDAI) for an outcome token (ex: Biden token), it sends tokens A to the auction contract.

fact: The auction contract then trades with the AMM, immediately updating the AMM price.
quote: This auction contract then makes a trade with the AMM such that the price given by the AMM is immediately updated.

fact: After the AMM trade, the auction contract owns the outcome tokens being bought and auctions them.
quote: The auction contract now owns the outcome tokens being bought and auctions them.

fact: The auction begins with the original trader as current winner and the bid price equal to what that trader paid.
quote: The auction starts with the original trader being the current winner and the bid price being the price paid by the original trader.

fact: If no one overbids, the original trader receives the outcome tokens, making the system function like a classic AMM with a small settlement delay.
quote: If no one overbids the original trader, those outcome tokens are simply given to the original trader and the system would have functioned as a classic AMM (except the small settlement delay).

fact: At the end of the bidding period, the winner receives the outcome tokens.
quote: At the end of the bidding period, the winner gets the outcome tokens.

fact: Any extra underlying tokens from overbidding are sent to the AMM and added to liquidity provider rewards.
quote: If there has been some overbidding, the auction contract will have some extra underlying tokens. Those are sent to the AMM contract and added to the rewards of the liquidity providers.

fact: Seer uses a bounded linear AMM because outcome token prices are bounded between 0 and 1.
quote: Since the price of outcome token shares are bounded between 0 and 1, we chose a bounded linear AMM (where the price increases linearly from 0 to 1)

fact: There is a minimum bid increment, for example 0.1%, to prevent trivial base-unit overbidding.
quote: there is a minimum bid increment (for example, 0.1%).

fact: Selling outcome tokens uses a descending auction where traders bid to accept the lowest amount of underlying tokens.
quote: Traders participate in a descending auction bidding to accept the lowest amount of underlying from their outcome tokens.
